usual_baseline: Core items (surgeon, date, procedure, findings) are near 100%. The same few items fail: blood loss 0–8% [2216, 2323, 2450, 2794], time of operation 0–9% [2216, 2319, 2524], elective/emergency 0–10% [1640, 2216, 2259], DVT prophylaxis 6% [2257]. Overall compliance about 50–72% [1600, 1276, 2319]; full compliance 4–7% [2274, 2844].
fix_that_works: A typed or electronic template with mandatory or drop-down fields. Overall 50% to 92% [1600]; below 80% to above 98% [2280]; 37.5% to 83.3% [2577]; 67% to 94% [2827]; full compliance 7% to 85% of template notes [2844]; 35% to 89% in template notes [2514]. Easy online access plus induction: 69% to 96.6% [2762].
fix_that_fails: Teaching or presentation alone: all items stayed well below standard, time 3% to 6.67% [2619]; knee 71% to 74%, hip 68% to 64% [1227]. Blood loss stayed at 8% despite a template [1136]. Templates are bypassed: use fell 45% to 28% [2169]; tonsillectomy proforma 33% [2118]. Gains fell at 24 months as new staff missed the template [1366].
consultant_advice: One of the most overdone audits, with 65 here and the same answer. Don't audit RCS items again. Audit whether a template is still used a year on and by new staff, or procedure-specific GIRFT items and whether notes reach the ward on time.
